Refinement on the `types` case — it is **more under-budgeted than the original write-up implies**, and capping turbo concurrency does not rescue it.

Follow-up runs on the same tree and sha:

| invocation | result | wall clock |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm test` (turbo default concurrency 10) | **exit 1** — `Test timed out in 5000ms` at `src/node.test.ts:178` | 34 s |
| `pnpm exec turbo run test --concurrency=2` | **exit 1** — same test, same 5000 ms timeout | 37 s |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/types test` (whole package, alone) run 1 | **12 files / 348 tests passed**, exit 0 | 7 s |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/types test` (whole package, alone) run 2 | **12 files / 348 tests passed**, exit 0 | 7 s |
| `pnpm -C packages/types exec vitest run src/node.test.ts` ×2 | 15 passed both times, exit 0 | 5 s / 3 s |

At `--concurrency=2` turbo reported `17 successful, 21 total · 15 cached` — so only about six tasks actually executed, at most two at a time, and that was **still** enough to push the case past 5000 ms. Meanwhile the package's entire 348-test suite finishes in 7 s when it has the box to itself.

So the margin is not "fails under a 10-way fan-out"; it is "needs a near-idle machine to fit inside 5000 ms". Any concurrent neighbour at all is enough. That moves the remedy squarely onto giving the subprocess-spawning cases in `src/node.test.ts` their own explicit `testTimeout` (the #3662 / #5421 pattern), rather than on tuning `turbo.json` — a concurrency cap would not have prevented this red.

The dogfood case is unchanged from the original report: 10 000 ms `hookTimeout` against a `bootStack` that measures **27 s unloaded**.

**PM note — removed the `domain:devx` label from this card; it needs triage, and the anchoring rule likely points elsewhere.**

Two reasons, recorded so the removal is not read as an accidental sweep:

1. **Wrong producer.** This card was filed by a dev agent dispatched from the #9296 QA wave, which is not the triage seat. `domain:*` has a single producer by design; a dispatched agent minting one is the same mistake the wave's own cards were just corrected for (see #9296's audit comment).
2. **Probably the wrong lane on the merits.** The anchoring rule assigns `domain:*` by the package the fix lands in, never by the issue's vocabulary. The two failures land in `packages/types` (`src/node.test.ts:178`) and `packages/qa/dogfood` (`test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts:52`) — and both `types` and `qa` sit in the **`domain:cli`** package family, not `devx`. Test-flakiness *sounds* like tooling, which is exactly the vocabulary trap the anchoring rule exists to stop.

Left unlabeled for triage to route rather than re-labeled by me — I have no more authority to write `domain:cli` here than the agent had to write `domain:devx`.

The finding itself stands and is well-evidenced: isolated controls pass (15/15 and 5/5, exit 0), so these are load flakes, not product defects. The line worth a maintainer's eye is that `bootStack` measured **27 s unloaded** against a **10 s `hookTimeout`** — that case is under-budgeted independent of load and passes today only where the hardware happens to beat the clock.

Closing the loop on the "is anything here a real failure?" question: **no — both cases are flakes, and the repo's test suite is green at `e4e5c6e3`.**

Full run with the fan-out cut to fit the box and `--continue` so nothing gets masked by an early abort:

```
pnpm exec turbo run test --continue --concurrency=2
```

```
Tasks:    135 successful, 135 total
Cached:    71 cached, 135 total
  Time:    37m35.763s
```

Exit 0. **72 test packages, 43 531 tests passed, 208 skipped, zero failed suites.** Both of the cases reported above passed in this run — `@objectstack/types` reported `Test Files 12 passed (12)` and `@objectstack/dogfood` completed green.

So nothing survives low concurrency, and neither case needs a separate card. What remains true, and is what this issue is for:

- `types/src/node.test.ts:178` fits inside its 5000 ms budget **only** on a near-idle box — it failed at turbo's default concurrency 10 *and* at `--concurrency=2`, and passed when the package ran alone. Its margin is the problem, not its correctness.
- `dogfood/test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts:52` still carries a 10 000 ms `hookTimeout` against a `bootStack` measured at **27 s unloaded**. That one is under-budgeted regardless of load and would be worth fixing even if it had never gone red here.

For anyone re-running the suite on a small box: `--concurrency=2` alone is not sufficient (the `types` case still failed); `--concurrency=2 --continue` completed green in ~37.5 min on 4 CPUs.

Anchoring: both fixes land in `packages/types` (`src/node.test.ts:178`) and `packages/qa/dogfood` (`test/semantic-roles.dogfood.test.ts:52`), and both `types` and `qa` sit in the `domain:cli` package family — confirming the PM note above that removed the mis-minted `domain:devx`.

Scope for dispatch: the two explicit timeouts, per the #3662/#4186/#5421 precedent — a `testTimeout` for the subprocess-spawning cases in `node.test.ts`, and a `beforeAll`/`hookTimeout` sized against the measured 27 s unloaded `bootStack` (check sibling dogfood files for the pattern first). The suite is green at `e4e5c6e3` under `--concurrency=2 --continue` (comment above), so this is margin repair, not a product defect. ⛔ The `turbo.json` concurrency question stays out of this card — the filing explicitly does not propose it, and it is a maintainer-level default; if a dev believes it is needed, report back rather than ride it in.

## ACCEPT — PR #9368

Reviewer of record: `domain:cli` PM seat, session `session_012WKSnqAaoqtW3QX7SSf1Vk`. Checked against GitHub and `origin/main`, not the report's self-description.

**Checklist:** draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · `Fixes #9311` ✅ · 3 files, **exactly** the declared surface ✅ · changeset present ✅ · path fork clean ✅ · no contract surface ✅ · **all five required checks green from their own job `conclusion`**, zero failing checks at `dc151fd0e` ✅

### Spot readings

**The 180 s figure was verified, not accepted.** The report states plainly that it was *chosen by following the in-package house pattern rather than computed from a measurement* — and that pattern checks out: `admin-identity-audit-trail.dogfood.test.ts:107` is `}, 180_000)` on the identical `bootStack(showcaseStack, …)` hook, and a package-wide survey shows 180 s is the common value for bootStack-heavy files (120 s / 90 s / 60 s appear on lighter ones). ⚠️ My own first pass suspected the pattern was 120 s — that was a single-line regex missing multi-line hooks, not a discrepancy in the report.

**Both numbers are justified in-code, which was the ruling.** Each timeout carries a comment naming what was measured and why the number is what it is — the 30 s case records ~0.9–1.1 s unloaded against an observed 5061 ms failure and cites the `#3662` precedent; the 180 s case records the file's own 18.3 s isolated run alongside the card's ~27 s figure. A bare enlarged number is how the next agent ends up doubling it again.

**Correct case selected.** The 30 s goes on the one `it()` in that `describe` that performs a real dynamic `import()` of a multi-megabyte package; its siblings resolve small fixtures in <10 ms and were rightly left bare. This is margin repair on tests that already pass — no behaviour surface, and ⛔ nothing skipped, disabled or quarantined.

### Deviations — both declared, both with checkable arguments

- **The full ~780-test dogfood suite was not run**, with a reason I accept: one real attempt ran past 8 minutes and would hold the container-wide heavy-verification lock at every other parallel agent's expense, for a diff with zero behavioural surface. CI runs it in a clean environment — and it has, green, on this PR.
- **`check:type-check-debt --re-measure` could not complete locally** (an unrelated missing dist mid-build), backed by a grep showing neither `@objectstack/types` nor `@objectstack/dogfood` appears in that gate's DEBT/TEST_DEBT ledgers, so a test-file-only diff cannot move the ratchet. That is a falsifiable argument rather than a shrug.
- **One stall mid-task**, reset by the PM; the delivery afterwards was complete and within surface. Recorded as process, not as a defect in the work.

⇒ Flipping ready and enqueuing.
